DEEP DIVE — GPS HISTORYGPS since 2022: peaked at 42%, now easing back to 37%19TAKEAWAYS—  GPS rose from about 30% in 2022 to a peak of 41.9% in 2024, then eased back to 34.5% in 2025 and sits at 37.1% today (FY2026) — two years of erosion, not a straight climb.—  BVP held 12-18% share through 2024, but 2025's decline is entirely Genuine (-EUR 71K) while BVP grew (+EUR 4K) — a Genuine-parts problem, not a BVP one.—  2022 doesn't reconcile with the previously computed series (EUR 261K vs EUR 186K net) — treat 2022 as directional; 2023-2025 corroborate closely.—  The FY2027 base is disputed: corrected-survival shrinks the parc to 3,645 (-2.4%); UIO V19 grows it to 3,992 (+6.9%) — worth agreeing which.

DEEP DIVE — GENUINE VS BVPGenuine vs BVP: 2025 breaks the pattern20TAKEAWAYS—  2025 is the only year since 2020 where Genuine and BVP move in opposite directions: Genuine EUR 341K → EUR 270K (-71K); BVP EUR 48K → EUR 52K (+4K). Every prior year they moved together.—  Not just a pricing effect: Genuine volume also fell (9,216 → 7,372 units) and breadth contracted (1,160 → 930 distinct genuine part numbers sold, -20%).—  BVP held up on every measure over the same year — units flat (4,036 → 4,052), SKU breadth grew (37 → 43) — so this isn't distributor-wide destocking, it's specific to Genuine.—  Worth cutting the 2025 genuine drop by category together before assuming it's competitive leakage — a concentrated cause (e.g. one model, one dealer) reads very differently from a broad-based one.

DEEP DIVE — COMPETITIVE CAPTUREWhere the gap is: competitive parts leaking to the aftermarket21Category202320242025Network (2025)Oil filter44.6%46.3%45.0%60.9%Fuel filter12.4%12.7%18.8%47.3%Air filter42.4%40.0%45.9%52.4%Brake pad11.7%11.1%15.6%29.8%Brake rotor22.4%25.4%36.1%54.9%—  The gap isn't new — Hungary has sat 15-35 points below network on brake pad, brake rotor and fuel filter capture in every one of the last three full years. Air filter is the one category near parity.—  Warranty claims (separate claims-system data, not part of the billing above) jumped from near-zero (FY2024: EUR 225) to EUR 102,418 (FY2026) — right where GPS started easing back. Worth checking if that's a genuine quality trend, a claims-logging change, or a campaign.QUESTIONS FOR US TO WORK THROUGH TOGETHER—  Brake pad/rotor capture has trailed the network by 15-35 points for three straight years — what's routing that work to independent garages?—  Warranty claims went from near-zero to over EUR 100K in two fiscal years — quality issue, claims-logging change, or a specific campaign?—  Which fleet number should FY2027 use — the ~4,000-unit growing view or the ~3,645-unit corrected-survival view?—  Genuine parts fell EUR 71K in 2025 while BVP grew EUR 4K — is genuine business moving to the aftermarket, or are dealers trading down within our own catalog?
